newsitem.title: USA: Bangor Hydro, farmer settle stressed cow suit.
newsitem.headline: Bangor Hydro, farmer settle stressed cow suit.

text.p: Farmer Richard Hall said he and his cows were feeling better even if they did not get everything they wanted in a court battle with an electric company, the Bangor Daily News said on Thursday.
Hall had filed suit against Bangor Hydro, claiming that his cows were producing less milk because they were being zapped by small amounts of electricity escaping into the ground from a utility line.

The two sides reached an out of court settlement this week, the exact terms of which were not released. Hall claimed a $350,000 loss between 1986 and 1992 due to reduced milk production but was not entirely satisifed with the settlement.
"I didn't get what I wanted or what I should have, but I think in the process what we did has helped a lot of farmers out and a lot of people," Hall told the newspaper.

The utility maintained that the cows' milk production dropped because Hall bought sick cows and did not know how to operate his feeding equipment properly. The company was "pleased with the results," an attorney said.
Similar suits have been filed elsewhere by farmers contending that cows are more sensitive than humans to stray electricity, which causes them to eat less and get sick more often.
